To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gap junctions regulate the coordination of signaling pathways involved in the regulation of CFTR activity and airway mucus hydration.

gap junctional communication between cells is required for the regulation of CFTR activity and ASL volume by the coordinated activation of PARs and ADO-Rs in the apical and basolateral membranes, respectively.
gap junctions coordinate the activation of CFTR by protease- and nucleotide-derived signals to maintain ASL volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of airway epithelial fluid transport by the activation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and gap junctional communication (GJC) in the context of the airway mucus layer.
the mechanisms that regulate airway hydration and mucus clearance in health and in disease.
the role of gap junctions in the regulation of CFTR activity and ASL volume by PGE₂.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coordinated activation of PARs and ADO-Rs at the apical and basolateral membranes, respectively, requires GJIC for ASL volume regulation.
GJIC plays an important role in coordinating the signaling network that maintains airway surface liquid homeostasis.
gap junctional intercommunication is required for the regulation of airway surface liquid homeostasis by the cystic fibrotic transmembrane conductant regulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coordinated regulation of CFTR by ADO-Rs and PARs requires gap junctional inter-cellular communication and that the failure of this communication results in the failure of the CFTR to hydrate mucus and clear the airway.
gap junctions coordinate the signaling network that regulates the CFTR-mediated Cl- secretion, which is critical for maintaining the ASL volume and hydration of mucus.

gap junctions are necessary to coordinate a signaling network involving CFTR, adenosine receptors, protease-activated receptor 2, and prostaglandin EP4 receptors, which together maintain airway surface fluid homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gap junctions coordinate the activation of CFTR and the regulation of ASL volume.
the coordination of signaling pathways by gap junctions is required for the regulation of ASL volume.
GJIC is a key mechanism for the regulation of ASL volume.
